title: Vesper and the Yearbook
premise: Sable Iversen, seventeen and effectively the parent of her two younger siblings, discovers that their late grandmother's recipe box holds instructions for a ritual called the Vesper, a generational bargain that has kept their dying mill town fed, safe, and strangely frozen in time. When she accidentally completes one of the 'recipes,' the siblings are bound into the tradition itself: each year someone must give up a year of their own future to keep the town alive, and this year's debt is due. Sable must decide whether to pay with her own longed-for graduation and freedom, uncover the truth that grandma spent decades secretly paying in secret to spare her children, or break the bargain and let the town face what it has been avoiding. In the end Sable chooses a third path — renegotiating the Vesper by offering shared, willing contributions from the whole community instead of stolen years from its children — saving both her siblings' futures and the town, though not without losing the last tangible piece of her grandmother.
about_author: Jude Ishikawa grew up in a fading Pacific Northwest timber town where every family had a recipe they refused to share. They write stories about kids who raise each other, and about the quiet magic hiding in ordinary kitchens.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishes her life: school, night shifts of parenting Dewey and Fern, mom working doubles at the cannery. She keeps a countdown calendar to graduation. Emotional beat: exhausted love, resentment she feels guilty about.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Cleaning out grandma's attic for extra cash, she finds the tin recipe box; cards are written in grandma's hand but call for impossible ingredients like 'one hour of patience, unspent.' Beat: curiosity cutting through grief.

chapters.title: Dewey's Experiment
chapters.summary: Dewey POV. Ten-year-old Dewey secretly tries a card — 'Sunday Bread for Missing People' — and the smell of it fills the house while their father, gone three years, is briefly heard on the porch. Beat: wonder laced with dread.

chapters.title: What the Town Won't Say
chapters.summary: Sable POV. At school she notices oddities: no new families since 1987, classmates who look exactly like their parents did. Her teacher deflects questions about the town charter. Beat: unease.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't Food
chapters.summary: Sable POV. The final card is labeled only 'Vesper — do not make alone.' Instructions reference a door under the grange hall and a debt 'come due.' Beat: the countdown calendar suddenly means something else.

chapters.title: Pulled Through
chapters.summary: All three siblings POV alternating. Following the card's steps half-jokingly at midnight, the kitchen wall opens; they step through into the Under-Town, a mirrored version of home where clocks run backward. Beat: vertigo, siblings gripping hands.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Sable POV. They meet the Keeper, an ageless woman tending a ledger of names and years. She informs them the Vesper is owed and, as eldest, Sable is now named. Beat: cold fear beneath polite conversation.

chapters.title: A Year, Measured
chapters.summary: Fern POV. Fern learns what payment means: a year of your future, lived inside the Under-Town while your body sleeps above. She finds grandma's name in the ledger — forty entries deep. Beat: betrayal and awe.

chapters.title: Home Again, Changed
chapters.summary: Sable POV. They're returned home; the kitchen is normal, but Sable's reflection ages a day each time she looks. Mom notices nothing. Beat: isolation — carrying a secret too big for bedtime.

chapters.title: Grandma's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Searching grandma's room, she finds hidden letters revealing grandma paid anonymously for thirty years so her children would never be chosen. Beat: reframing everything Sable thought she knew about sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: The Keeper appears in a dream to all three siblings: the town's protection lapses at harvest unless a year is paid. Beat: deadline established — six weeks.

chapters.title: Sable Says No
chapters.summary: Sable POV. She refuses to pay and refuses to let Dewey or Fern volunteer. She starts researching how the Vesper began. Beat: defiance hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Miss Aldous Remembers
chapters.summary: Dual POV with elderly Miss Aldous, the oldest resident. She recalls the flood year of 1952 when the first Vesper was struck — the town traded its future to survive the winter. Beat: history as warning.

chapters.title: The Grange Hall Basement
chapters.summary: Sable and Dewey POV. They break into the sealed basement and find the original contract, signed by every founding family — including the Iversens. Beat: complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Fern Runs
chapters.summary: Fern POV. Terrified, Fern decides the simplest fix is to volunteer herself and sneaks toward the Under-Town door. Beat: love expressed as self-erasure.

chapters.title: Stopped at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Sable catches Fern at the door; their fight cracks open years of Sable's guilt over being 'the parent.' Beat: raw confrontation, then tenderness.

chapters.title: Mom's Night Off
chapters.summary: Mom POV. Exhausted, mom comes home early and finds the recipe box out. She admits she always knew something kept the town 'too easy' but chose not to look. Beat: the adults' willful blindness named.

chapters.title: Telling the Truth
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Family meeting: Sable lays out everything. Mom weeps, Dewey takes notes, Fern asks the hard question — if the town dies, where do they go? Beat: the family becomes a team.

chapters.title: Reading the Fine Print
chapters.summary: Dewey POV. Dewey, the detail kid, deciphers the contract's clauses and finds an overlooked line: terms may be 'renegotiated by unanimous consent of the living signatories.' Beat: hope with a catch — most signatory families are gone.

chapters.title: The Descendants
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Sable maps which classmates descend from founding families: Priya Chandrasekaran, Theo Marsh, quiet Caleb Ostrander. She starts asking them strange questions. Beat: recruiting allies, risking ridicule.

chapters.title: Priya's Price
chapters.summary: Priya POV. Priya reveals her family's version: her grandmother lost her wedding day, her mother her twenties — years eaten quietly. She agrees to help. Beat: solidarity between girls carrying invisible debts.

chapters.title: Caleb Knows More
chapters.summary: Caleb POV. Caleb's family are the Keepers' hereditary servants; he's been leaving offerings since childhood. He warns renegotiation requires a 'willing gift greater than the taken thing.' Beat: the cost becomes clear.

chapters.title: Harvest Approaches
chapters.summary: Rotating sibling POVs. Two weeks left; the town grows subtly wrong — apples ripening black, streetlights burning at noon. Beat: mounting dread made visible.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Story
chapters.summary: Keeper POV (first time). She was the first child ever paid, in 1952, and has tended the ledger for seventy years because no one ever came back for her. Beat: villain reframed as victim.

chapters.title: A Gift Greater Than Years
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Sable realizes the counter-offer: not one person's stolen future, but everyone's willing present — memory, labor, care, freely given. But it needs nearly the whole town to consent. Beat: the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Asking the Town
chapters.summary: Sable and Priya POV. They go door to door with the truth. Some slam doors; others, like Miss Aldous, sign immediately. Beat: courage met with both rejection and grace.

chapters.title: The Naysayers
chapters.summary: Theo Marsh POV. Theo's father leads the opposition — the Vester bargain built his business and he'll protect it. He threatens Sable's family directly. Beat: human antagonist emerges from the system.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Dewey POV. Someone burns part of the recipe box; the Vesper card survives only because Fern had copied it. Beat: loss, and the siblings' preparedness paying off.

chapters.title: Mom Signs First
chapters.summary: Mom POV. Mom publicly signs the new covenant at the diner counter, daring the town to call her crazy. Beat: the parent finally standing beside her kids.

chapters.title: Quorum
chapters.summary: Sable POV. On the final day they count signatures: one short of unanimity among living descendants. The missing signature is Theo's father. Beat: crisis point.

chapters.title: Theo's Choice
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Theo confronts his father with the ledger showing the Marsh family's paid years — including the year his father took from Theo's older brother, still sleeping in the Under-Town. Beat: private reckoning.

chapters.title: The Last Signature
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Theo's father signs at dusk, not from goodness but because Theo shames him with love. Quorum reached. Beat: victory that tastes complicated.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: All allies POV rotating. The group enters the Under-Town together to present the new covenant before the harvest bell. Beat: collective bravery, the town literally walking into its own past.

chapters.title: The Keeper Refuses
chapters.summary: Sable POV. The Keeper rejects the covenant — a willing gift can't erase seventy years of her stolen life. She rings the bell early. Beat: climax begins; the bargain starts collapsing.

chapters.title: Come Back For Her
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Sable offers the Keeper what no one offered in seventy years: a place above, a name in the new ledger, a family. 'You were a child they didn't come back for. We came back.' Beat: emotional climax — love against duty.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The old contract burns; the sleeping paid years begin returning to their owners across town. The Keeper, aging rapidly into her true years, chooses to stay and help transition. Beat: release.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Above
chapters.summary: Fern POV. The town wakes changed — color returns, a moving truck arrives with new neighbors, time moves forward. Some mourn the safety of stasis. Beat: bittersweet renewal.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Sable walks at graduation, the countdown calendar finally finished — not served, but celebrated. Mom, Dewey, Fern, Priya, Theo, and the Keeper (as 'Aunt Vera') watch. Beat: earned joy.

chapters.title: Recipes Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Dewey POV. Dewey rewrites the recipe box with real recipes plus one blank card labeled 'for whatever comes next.' The family cooks Sunday bread together, for no reason but hunger and love. Beat: warmth, ordinary magic reclaimed.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Sable POV, epilogue. A year later, Sable leaves for college but promises to return each harvest — not to pay, but to celebrate. Final image: the town's evening bell rings freely, and no one owes anything. Beat: peace, identity chosen rather than inherited.
